messages:
Sam Rivera: Hey team — unboxed my company MacBook Pro (M2 Max) and trying to enroll in Jamf. During the MDM step it gets to "Creating FileVault recovery key..." then the UI says "Uploading profile..." and just spins for 10+ minutes. Any quick things to try?

Alex Cho: @Sam Rivera welcome aboard! :wave: Two quick checks: 1) disconnect any USB hubs/external monitors and retry, 2) try on the office Wi‑Fi (sometimes home networks block the escrow endpoint). Did you get the "Create local recovery key" option or an iCloud one?

Sam Rivera: It was the local recovery key option. I do have a USB‑C hub + external display attached. Trying to detach now.

IT Ops: Removing peripherals is a good start. Also can you paste the tail of /var/log/jamf.log after the attempt? Example command: `sudo tail -n 100 /var/log/jamf.log` — just paste the relevant 5–10 lines.

Sam Rivera: Removed hub + monitor, retried, still stalls. Paste of jamf.log snippet:
```
2026-03-23 14:12:05.123 jamf[12345]: ProfileInstallation: started
2026-03-23 14:12:12.546 jamf[12345]: EscrowService: sending escrow request
2026-03-23 14:12:15.789 jamf[12345]: EscrowService: HTTP/1.1 401 Unauthorized
2026-03-23 14:12:16.001 jamf[12345]: MDMProfileInstallationError: Escrow failed (401)
```

Jamf Bot: Jamf enrollment attempt logged for device serial XXXXXXX at 2026-03-23T14:12:05Z — status: failed (Escrow 401)

Carmen Liu: If you see a 401 on escrow, that usually means our escrow cert/token rotation didn't match older agent tokens. Two options: 1) reboot and try enrollment again (client will fetch new cert), or 2) IT Ops can manually generate a temporary personal recovery key and push it via a Jamf policy to complete escrow. Before that, run `sudo fdesetup status` and paste output so we know if FileVault is already enabled.

Alex Cho: Also check network path — if you were using the hub as a gateway it can mess with proxy headers. Try direct Wi‑Fi or tether phone briefly. If still fails, @IT Ops will escalate to create a manual key.

Sam Rivera: Running `sudo fdesetup status` gives: `FileVault is On.` jamf.log shows the same 401. I'm on home Wi‑Fi (no corporate VPN).

IT Ops: We rotated the escrow cert in the early morning maintenance window — that could explain the 401. Try a reboot and then re-run the enrollment flow (no hubs attached). If it still fails, reply here and we'll create a one‑time recovery key and stage a Jamf policy to escrow it. ETA ~20 minutes to generate and push.

Sam Rivera: Rebooted, retried enrollment on office Wi‑Fi (connected at 14:35). Enrollment completed successfully and the console shows the recovery key escrowed. Thanks for the quick help everyone! :tada:

Alex Cho: Awesome — glad it worked. Ping us if anything else in the first week. Also welcome to the Infra crew! :raised_hands: 

IT Ops: Marking as resolved. Will follow up in Jamf with a note about the cert rotation impact on fresh enrolls.

Sam Rivera: Thanks all! 👍
